# Authoring `@pantoken/components`

`@pantoken/components` is the semantic RSCSS CSS API — a parameterized generator, not hand-written
CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.

## Automatic user preferences

User preferences are intrinsic behavior, not modifiers. Gate decorative transitions and animations
with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` in each record so standalone sheets and shadow styles
follow the same policy. Keep loading and progress indicators visible when animation stops, and
apply state changes immediately. Interaction behaviors must also respect the live preference:
don't smooth-scroll, delay removal for a skipped fade, or hide progress behind a mount animation.
Do not shorten loading timeouts or cancel announcements in the name of reducing motion.

Token sheets handle color preferences in the active theme's scope. `prefers-contrast: more`
strengthens nonzero border widths and focus rings; `less` removes decorative elevation color without
reducing text contrast. Keep semantic text/status colors and explicit light/dark pins intact.
Links gain an underline in more-contrast mode, including normally unstyled links.

Reduced transparency composites translucent surface tokens over an opaque semantic background.
Remove backdrop blur in that mode, and use opaque muted colors rather than whole-control opacity for
disabled states. Keep intentionally empty backgrounds, image effects, and visibility transitions:
they aren't interchangeable with translucent component chrome. New surface expressions need coverage
in the token preference generator and a real-browser check.

In forced colors, keep browser adjustment on surrounding components and text. Masked glyphs can use
`forced-color-adjust: preserve-parent-color` on the painter itself, with system-color fills. Give
gradient text a solid system-color fallback, and keep selected states visible without shadows.
Native progress needs authored value parts and a CSS-owned indeterminate segment: suppressing CSS
animations alone doesn't stop the browser's built-in loading animation. Check actual rendered pixels,
native range semantics, and live preference changes, including RTL.

## Source layout

- `src/components/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
- `src/components/<name>/members/<member>/index.ts` + `<member>.css` — a promoted sub-component (see

- `src/utilities/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`UTILITIES`).

`Table.Row`, `Menu.Item`, …), promote it to its own record instead of documenting it as a `@part`
bullet on the parent:

- New files: `src/components/<parent>/members/<member>/<member>.css` + `index.ts`, same shape as any
  other record (`defineComponent`, registered in `COMPONENTS`, exported from `src/index.ts`).
- The record's cssdoc name is **dotted**: `@component <parent>.<member>` (e.g. `@component menu.item`)

  have a same-named part (`menu.item` vs `side-nav-bar.item`), which a bare `item`/`item` collision
  would break for the `providers`-indexed cross-file `@memberOf`/`@structure` resolution. The TS
  identifier stays camelCase (`menuItem`/`menuItemCss`), since a dot isn't legal there anyway.

# @pantoken/plugin-custom-components

Custom, cssdoc-documented component rules for downstream consumers.

This package currently ships:

- An extra-small `--instui-breakpoints-xs: 20em` declaration in the aggregate stylesheet
- `cardRules(prefix?)` and `card.css` as deprecated compatibility aliases; use `cardCss` from `@pantoken/components`
- `banner` rules (the plugin output)
- `agent-shell` rules (the plugin output)
- `button-set` rules (the plugin output)

## Install

```sh
npm i @pantoken/plugin-custom-components
```

Also available as `pantoken/custom-components`.

## Usage

Use the plugin to append the custom component sheet to token CSS output:

```ts
import { toCss } from "@pantoken/css";
import { byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens";
import { customComponents } from "@pantoken/plugin-custom-components";

const css = toCss(byTheme("rebrand"), { plugins: [customComponents()] });
```

Import the built stylesheet directly when you only need the static CSS:

```ts
import "@pantoken/plugin-custom-components/custom-components.css";
```

Or import one component:

```ts
import "@pantoken/plugin-custom-components/card.css";
```

## API

- `customComponents(options?)` — returns a CSS plugin with `position: "append" | "prepend"`.
- `breakpointDeclarations()` — returns the extra-small viewport token declaration.
- `cardRules(prefix?)` — deprecated alias for the `@pantoken/components` Card stylesheet.
- `bannerRules(prefix?)` — returns the banner rules as CSS text.
- `agentShellRules(prefix?)` — returns the agent-shell rules as CSS text.
- `buttonSetRules(prefix?)` — returns the button-set rules as CSS text.
- `./custom-components.css` — aggregate stylesheet export.
- `./card.css`, `./banner.css`, `./agent-shell.css`, `./button-set.css` — per-component stylesheet exports.

## cssdoc

`./model.json` publishes the documented component records as a `CssDocEntry[]` model. Add it
to your `cssdoc.json` `providers` so a consumer project resolves these classes/modifiers:

```jsonc
{
  "providers": [{ "path": "./node_modules/@pantoken/plugin-custom-components/model.json" }],
  // Built with a different prefix than the default "instui-" (or none)? Rewrite it — `to` is used
  // verbatim, no separator assumed:
  //   "prefix": { "from": "instui-", "to": "acme-" }
}
```

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
  [-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns core CSS
  correctness; cssdoc owns documentation comments. `lint:css` and `lint:cssdoc` run in `ready`, and
  both are wired into the `vite.config.ts` staged hook.

`vpr docs:dev` builds interactions before staging its browser bundles. The interactions build task
declares its workspace dependencies' builds as prerequisites, so `@pantoken/utils` is built even
when its `dist` output is missing. Run `vp run @pantoken/interactions#build` rather than invoking
`scripts/build-iife.ts` directly when prerequisites haven't been built.
CSS generation also declares both runtime and development workspace builds as prerequisites:
its generator imports `@pantoken/plugin-props-minify` from development dependencies. Keep these
prerequisites on the generator task so standalone generation and docs startup use the same order.

## Accessibility evidence in the docs build

The docs build keeps the checked-in evidence (`docs/public/accessibility/results.json`) current, so
the `## Accessibility` tables on each CSS API page match the code that ships. The `accessibility`
asset task (`docs/scripts/accessibility-refresh.ts`, run by `docs:assets`) fingerprints every audited
record from its CSS and examples, built stylesheet and behavior script, and the inputs every page
shares (tokens, base, focus, elevation, the automatica11y version, and the audit harness). It
re-audits only records whose fingerprint differs from the one stored in the snapshot and merges the
results back, so an unchanged tree is a fast no-op.

- `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:accessibility` refreshes stale records. `--check` (via
  `docs:accessibility:check`) reports them without auditing; `--all` re-audits everything; `--adopt`
  stamps current fingerprints onto existing evidence when you know the inputs didn't change the results.
- Commit the updated snapshot with the change that caused it. The `component-accessibility` CI job
  re-audits stale records and fails when the committed snapshot differs.
- On CI (or with `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_INSTALL_BROWSER=1`) the refresh provisions the audit browser
  when it needs one. `docs:dev` sets `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT=skip` so a dev server never starts an audit.
- The tables are raw HTML in the generated page. The segmenter classifies them as `audit` blocks, so
  their visible text (headings, pill labels, details) enters `l10n/docs.api.pot` through the normal API
  translation pipeline while markup and `<code>` selectors stay verbatim. The fixed labels live in
  `ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT_STRINGS` in `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.

`vp run audit:components` is an explicit, uncached full audit task, separate from `ready` (the docs build re-audits only stale records; see above). It uses the

component examples. It doesn't send examples to a remote audit service.
The task first runs the shared `build:all` prerequisite, restoring the complete workspace build
graph in dependency order. A fresh checkout or restored CI task cache doesn't contain package
outputs until those tasks run; building only components, CSS, and interactions can leave their
build-time workspace dependencies missing.

The tool requires Chrome or Chromium. Check setup with
`vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor`. If a browser is missing, explicitly opt into
its download with `vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor --install-browser`.
